channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Canadian Dollar strengthens as Trump pauses 50% tariffs, Oil prices climb
item.description: USD/CAD declines on Wednesday and trades around 1.3810 at the time of writing, down 0.62% on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA keeps hawkish bias on inflation – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports the Reserve Bank of Australia remains concerned about inflation, with Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser saying further rate hikes cannot be ruled out.

item.title: Bank of England: Rate hold baseline with conflict risks – Societe Generale
item.description: Sam Cartwright at Societe Generale argues recent easing in United Kingdom (UK) services inflation and labour market loosening support the Bank of England’s wait-and-see stance. The baseline view is Bank Rate stays at 3.75% through 2026 to restrain underlying inflation.

item.title: United States Dollar Index falls as US Treasury doubles long-dated debt buybacks
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) comes under fresh selling pressure on Wednesday as longer-term US Treasury yields fall sharply following the Treasury Department’s decision to expand its buyback operations.

item.title: South Korean Won: Growth-driven recovery offers policy lesson – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING explains that Korea’s earlier massive portfolio outflows and a weaker Korean Won (KRW) pushed USD/KRW to 1560 in June, despite a large current account surplus.

item.title: Fed Minutes expected to shed light on the depth of FOMC hawkish split
item.description: The United States (US) Federal Reserve (Fed) will release the Minutes of the July Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Wednesday.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Policy support eyed as growth slows – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay, Dr. Henry Hao and Moses Lim note that China’s July data showed weaker Industrial Production and Retail Sales, underscoring fading momentum at the start of Q3.

item.title: Euro rises to June highs as falling US Treasury yields weigh on US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD climbs sharply on Wednesday, reaching its highest level since June as the US Dollar (USD) comes under fresh selling pressure following the US Treasury’s announcement that it will increase buybacks of longer-dated government debt.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Shallow uptrend risk into next year – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes AUD/USD is currently on the back foot, with the Australian Dollar the weakest G10 currency on a one-day view. Despite market doubts, Rabobank still expects one more Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) rate hike this year.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Stability-focused BI stance – UOB
item.description: UOB economist Enrico Tanuwidjaja notes that Bank Indonesia (BI) kept the BI Rate at 5.75% in August, prioritizing Rupiah and macro-financial stability over growth.

item.title: Gold climbs over 2% as US Treasury buyback plan pressures long-term yields
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rallies on Wednesday as a softer US Dollar (USD) and a sharp pullback in long-term US Treasury yields help the metal recover all the previous day’s losses. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,458, up over 2.5% on the day.

item.title: US Treasury doubles some long-dated debt buybacks to support liquidity
item.description: The United States (US) Department of the Treasury (US Treasury) announced on Wednesday that it will double the size of some of its buyback operations aimed at supporting liquidity in the longer-dated Treasury securities market.

item.title: United Kingdom: Constrained backdrop and BoE risks – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Sam Cartwright argues that a new UK Prime Minister has not altered the constrained fiscal backdrop, limiting ambitions on housebuilding, social care, investment and defence.

item.title: China: Policy support and structural shifts – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists review July data and the latest China Politburo guidance. Retail sales and Fixed Asset Investment softened, while Industrial Production and exports were supported by AI-related and green technology demand.

item.title: Euro: Domestic demand resilience supports EUR – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde’s warning that Europe’s post-war growth model is eroding as global trade fragments and cheap energy fades.

item.title: Canada: EU protectionist shift challenges diversification – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada’s (NBC) Angelo Katsoras argues that Canada’s push to diversify exports away from the United States (US) toward the European Union (EU) faces growing obstacles as EU industrial policy turns more protectionist.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains as US Dollar retreats ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: USD/JPY edges lower on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) loses momentum and retreats toward the June lows touched earlier this week. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 159.10, down 0.32% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed minutes watched as rate doubts grow – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke says markets will scrutinize the latest Fed minutes for clues on how close policymakers remain to another rate hike after weaker US labour and inflation data reduced expectations for a hike by year-end.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Policy continuity supports currency – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts Galvin Chia and Kunal Kundu note that Bank Indonesia kept the BI rate at 5.75%, with deposit and lending facility rates unchanged, reinforcing Rupiah stability and inflation control.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD bounces to $4,370, but upside momentum is fading
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades moderately higher on Wednesday and returns to the $4,370 area, after finding buyers near the $4,300 area on Tuesday.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Needs decisive break above $85 for fresh advance
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trade 0.55% higher at around $84.80 during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: Silver has rebounded to $63, but inflationary risks hold buyers back
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) stabilizes around $63.45 on Wednesday, up 0.16% on the day at the time of writing. The white metal is attempting to regain its footing after hitting an intraday low of $62.19, initially extending the pullback that followed Tuesday’s rejection from the $66.50 area.

item.title: British Pound: Carry appeal keeps Sterling resilient as BoE stays on hold – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner, citing UK economist James Smith, notes that July United Kingdom (UK) Consumer Price Index (CPI) had limited impact on EUR/GBP, with benign food inflation and only a modest uptick in the Bank of England’s core services measure to 3.8%.

item.title: US Dollar: Exposure normalizes as real rates fall – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that international investors are aggressively cutting Dollar exposure as real-yield support erodes following the July FOMC meeting. The bank sees the Dollar decline as a normalization of previously extreme U.S. asset holdings rather than a collapse in U.S. exceptionalism.

item.title: Indian Rupee trades lower, RBI remains on standby to limit downside
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) remains vulnerable against the US Dollar (USD), close to its two-week low at around 95.75.

item.title: Australian Dollar ticks up from intra-week lows with all eyes on Fed minutes
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD)has bounced up from intra-week lows against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, although the daily chart remains negative.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: More upside expected above 1.3570
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is up 0.2% to near 1.3557 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA seen sidelined on softer wages – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports the Australian Dollar is underperforming as bond yields fall after Q2 wage growth matched expectations. Haddad argues this outcome will keep the RBA on hold, with private sector wage gains at a four‑year low.

item.title: Euro steadies against Japanese Yen as ECB, BoJ rate-hike bets collide
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 184.70 on Wednesday at the time of writing, edging 0.03% lower on the day.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Election risks then renewed gains – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank FX analysts Norman Liebke and Michael Pfister see the Brazilian Real (BRL) supported by the Brazilian Central Bank’s (BCB) hawkish stance and still-elevated real interest rates.
